title: Trump honors Rudy Giuliani with presidential medal of freedom
summary:
President’s former lawyer, disbarred over effort to overturn 2020 election result, receives top civilian honor

Donald Trump awarded Rudy Giuliani, his former personal attorney who was…

blocks.text: Donald Trump awarded Rudy Giuliani, his former personal attorney who was disbarred for his efforts to help the US president overturn 2020 election results, with the presidential medal of freedom on Tuesday.

The presidential medal of freedom is one of the highest civilian awards in the US, typically given to individuals who contribute to world peace, the national interest of the US or significant cultural endeavors.
On Monday, Giuliani, 82, told Steve Bannon that the US president would give him the award on Tuesday , more than a year after Trump announced he would award it to him.
“I’m, of course, very, very humbled and very honored not only to receive it but to receive it from him,” Giuliani told Bannon.

On Trump’s schedule, the award presentation was “closed press”, meaning no media were present. But before the ceremony, the White House posted a compilation video of Giuliani, saying he left an “undeniable mark on American history”.
After the ceremony, Andrew Giuliani, the son of Rudy Giuliani, told reporters it was “incredibly special” to see his father receive the award from Trump.

“I think what Rudy Giuliani has done over the last six years will go down in history as one of the most important legal jobs that has ever been done by any attorney. To defend the president of the United States against some of the evil forces that are out there, I am so proud of my father,” Andrew Giuliani said.
Giuliani served as the mayor of New York during the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks. For his leadership, he became a globally recognized figure, earning the nickname “America’s mayor”.
After serving as mayor, he ran for the Republican presidential nomination in 2008, but dropped out of the race after underperforming in early primaries.

In the decades after 9/11, Giuliani’s reputation suffered several blows, in part because of his loyalty to Trump. For promoting Trump’s false claims of election fraud, Giuliani lost his license to practice law.
He also settled a multimillion-dollar defamation suit filed by election workers Ruby Freeman and her daughter Wandrea “Shaye” Moss after he falsely accused them of election fraud.
Giuliani filed for bankruptcy in 2023 after he settled the $148m defamation suit, though a judge later dismissed the bankruptcy suit.
In 2025 Giuliani also settled a long-running, billion-dollar lawsuit filed by voting machine manufacturer Dominion Voting Systems.
Giuliani also pleaded not guilty to state charges in Georgia and Arizona stemming from efforts to overturn the 2020 election, though both cases were eventually dismissed.

In his second term, Trump has awarded the presidential medal of freedom posthumously to Charlie Kirk, the conservative activist and co-founder of Turning Point USA, as well as Welles Crowther, a stock trader and volunteer firefighter who died during 9/11 while rescuing people.
